title: Where a Function Rises and Falls

steps.body: Read a graph left to right, like a sentence. A function is **increasing** where the graph climbs and **decreasing** where it falls. We name the stretches by their **x-values** — the inputs where the behavior happens — never by the heights.
A negative slope is a falling function.

widget.prompt: A sits at x = −2 on y = x². Set the gap to 1 and read the sign of the slope.
widget.successFeedback: The slope is −3: negative, and the function is FALLING across that interval even though y = x² is famously a rising parabola. Rising and falling are local facts, and the sign of the slope is how you read them.
widget.lowFeedback: The gap is under 1 — B has not reached x = −1 yet.
widget.highFeedback: The gap is over 1 — B has passed x = −1.

predict.prompt: You'll build the secant from A at x = -2 out to B at x = -1 on y = x². Compared with the tangent slope AT A (-4), the secant's slope will be…
predict.reveal: The secant's slope is (f(-1) − f(-2))/1 = -3, against -4 for the tangent at A. On a curve whose slope keeps growing, the stretch out to B crosses steeper ground than A itself — so the average beats the value at the start.

cml.actionGoal: Shrink the interval between two points and compare secant slope with the limiting tangent slope.

steps.body: Between its two turning points this curve **falls**: it is decreasing on the interval −1 < x < 1. Outside them it rises. Notice the answer is a set of **inputs** — 'decreasing on (−1, 1)' — even though your eye tracks the heights.

explanationVariants: The graph falls exactly between its peak at x = −1 and its valley at x = 1: decreasing on (−1, 1).
Pick test inputs: from x = −0.5 to x = 0.5 the outputs drop (1.375 down to −1.375), and this holds across all of (−1, 1).

widget.prompt: On which interval is y = x³ − 3x decreasing?

commonBuilds.feedback: That interval is named by the HEIGHTS of the turning points (2 and −2). Intervals use x-values: the fall spans x = −1 to x = 1.
Past x = 1 the curve has already turned back UP — it's increasing there. The fall is between the turns, on (−1, 1).

widget.missFeedback: Decreasing runs BETWEEN the turning inputs x = −1 and x = 1: the interval (−1, 1).
widget.successFeedback: Right — the fall runs between the two turning inputs x = −1 and x = 1.

explanationVariants: The vertex of y = −(x − 2)² + 9 is at x = 2; an opening-down parabola rises up to its vertex and falls after: increasing on (−∞, 2).
Test inputs: g(0) = 5 < g(1) = 8 < g(2) = 9, climbing all the way to x = 2 — then g(3) = 8 starts the fall.

widget.prompt: On which interval is y = −(x − 2)² + 9 increasing?

commonBuilds.feedback: After x = 2 this downward parabola FALLS. It increases on the way up to the vertex, (−∞, 2).
9 is the vertex's HEIGHT. Increasing/decreasing intervals are sets of x-values: (−∞, 2).

widget.missFeedback: This downward parabola climbs UP TO its vertex at x = 2: increasing on (−∞, 2).
widget.successFeedback: Yes — it climbs toward the vertex at x = 2, then falls.

explanationVariants: y = |x − 3| + 1 is a V with corner at x = 3: it falls until x = 3 and rises afterward, so decreasing on (−∞, 3).
Test: at x = 0, 2, 3 the outputs are 4, 2, 1 — dropping; past 3 they climb again.

widget.prompt: On which interval is y = |x − 3| + 1 decreasing?

commonBuilds.feedback: To the right of the corner the V climbs. The descent is the LEFT arm, (−∞, 3).
1 is the corner's height, not its input. The corner sits at x = 3, so the fall is (−∞, 3).

widget.missFeedback: The left arm of the V descends into the corner at x = 3: decreasing on (−∞, 3).
widget.successFeedback: Right — the left arm of the V descends into the corner at x = 3.

explanationVariants: Compute a few outputs of y = x³ − 3x past x = 1: f(1) = −2, f(2) = 2, f(3) = 18 — climbing without bound, so increasing on (1, ∞).
After its valley at x = 1 the cubic turns up and never turns again (only two turning points exist, at x = ±1).
hints: The curve's only turns are at x = −1 and x = 1 — what must it do after the last turn?
Evaluate f at x = 1, 2, 3 and watch the direction.
f(1) = −2, f(2) = 2, f(3) = 18: rising from x = 1 onward.

widget.prompt: What is y = x³ − 3x doing on the interval (1, ∞)?

options.label: Increasing the whole way
options.feedback: Yes — after the valley at x = 1 the outputs climb forever: −2, 2, 18, …

options.label: Decreasing the whole way
options.feedback: Check outputs: f(1) = −2 but f(2) = 2 — that's a climb. The fall happened BEFORE x = 1, on (−1, 1).

options.label: It turns again at x = 2
options.feedback: f(2) = 2 being positive doesn't make x = 2 a turn — outputs keep growing (f(3) = 18). This cubic's only turns are at x = ±1.

takeaways: Increasing = graph climbs left-to-right; decreasing = it falls.
Report intervals with x-values, never heights.
Turning points are where the behavior switches.
steps.teaser: Next: the turning points themselves — peaks and valleys, local and absolute.

concept.body: Trace left to right. Climbing = increasing, falling = decreasing. Name the stretch by the x-values where it happens.

explanationVariants: y = x² falls until its vertex at x = 0, then rises: decreasing on (−∞, 0).
Outputs at x = −2, −1, 0 are 4, 1, 0 — dropping toward the vertex.

widget.prompt: On which interval is y = x² decreasing?

options.feedback: Right — the left half of the parabola descends into the vertex.
The right half CLIMBS: 0, 1, 4, … The descent is the left half, (−∞, 0).
